html:
The Battle of Didgori was fought on 12 August 1121 west of Tbilisi, where the army of King David IV routed a much larger coalition of Seljuk Turkish forces.

David's troops, including Kipchak horsemen and Western crusader volunteers, used the hilly ground and a surprise attack to break the enemy. The victory ended the Seljuk threat to Georgia and let David take Tbilisi, held by Muslim emirs since the 700s, the next year. It opened a century in which Georgia expanded into Armenia and Shirvan. Georgians call it the miraculous victory, and it is marked every year on 12 August with a festival on the field.
sum: The Battle of Didgori was fought on 12 August 1121 west of Tbilisi, where the army of King David IV routed a much larger coalition of Seljuk Turkish forces.
